title: Open scheme tests give monomorphy and etale composite charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $O,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $j:O\to Y$ be a morphism. Suppose that for every $S$-scheme $H$ and every $c:h_H\to Y$, the sheaf fibre product $h_H\times_YO$ is represented by a scheme $O_H$, whose projection to $H$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Here $h_H(K)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(K,H)$, and fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with scheme fibre products as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $j$ is injective on sections over every scheme: for $a_1,a_2\in O(H)$ with $j(a_1)=j(a_2)$ one has $a_1=a_2$. Thus $j$ is a monomorphism of these sheaves. Each $O_H\to H$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For every representable etale chart $v:h_V\to O$ with $V$ a scheme, the composite $jv:h_V\to Y$ is representable etale. More precisely, for every $c:h_H\to Y$ its scheme test is canonically $h_V\times_Yh_H\cong h_V\times_O h_{O_H}$; the scheme representing the right side has etale projection to $O_H$, and its projection to $H$ is the composite of that map with $O_H\to H$.

source.place: Tag 02WK (lemma-composition-representable-transformations-property), specialized to an open inclusion and an etale chart; scheme inputs: morphisms.tex Tags 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale), and schemes.tex Tag 01L7 (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms).

proof.text: Fix an $S$-scheme $H$ and $a_1,a_2\in O(H)$ with common image $c\in Y(H)$. A section $a$ defines the natural transformation $h_H\to O$ sending $t:K\to H$ to $a|_t$; evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_H$ is its inverse. Thus the two compatible pairs $(\mathrm{id}_H,a_i)$ give two maps $s_i:H\to O_H$ over $H$, under the assumed representing isomorphism $h_{O_H}\cong h_H\times_YO$. To see this correspondence explicitly, a natural transformation $h_H\to h_{O_H}$ is the map obtained by evaluating at $\mathrm{id}_H$, since naturality forces its value on $t$ to be composition with $t$. The projection $p:O_H\to H$ is an open immersion, hence a monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. Since $p s_1=p s_2=\mathrm{id}_H$, we have $s_1=s_2$, and evaluation of the $O$-projection gives $a_1=a_2$.

source.place: Tag 01L7 (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms), applied to the scheme test; spaces.tex, discussion following definition-immersion.

proof.text: For any sheaf $F$ and maps $u_1,u_2:F\to O$ satisfying $j u_1=j u_2$, step 1 applied to $u_1(x),u_2(x)$ for every scheme $H$ and $x\in F(H)$ gives equality of all components. Hence $u_1=u_2$, which is precisely that $j$ is a monomorphism of sheaves.

source.place: Discussion following definition-immersion: immersions are monomorphisms.

proof.text: For every scheme test $c:h_H\to Y$, the given scheme map $p:O_H\to H$ is an open immersion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] to obtain that $p$ is etale.

Compatible-pair functors are sheaves: glue each component by its sheaf axiom; equality of the images follows by uniqueness of gluing. Thus these functors realize the sheaf pullbacks. Fix the representable etale map $v:h_V\to O$ and a scheme test $c:h_H\to Y$. Let $r:h_{O_H}\to O$ be the other projection of $h_{O_H}\cong h_H\times_YO$. By the scheme-test definition in [def-trf-algebraic-space], $h_V\times_O h_{O_H}$ is represented by a scheme $W$ and its projection $q:W\to O_H$ is etale. The required comparison is explicit: on each test scheme $K$, send $(x,t)\in V(K)\times H(K)$ with $jv(x)=c(t)$ to $(x,(t,v(x)))$. Its inverse sends $(x,(t,o))$, where $v(x)=o$ and $c(t)=j(o)$, to $(x,t)$. Restrictions preserve both formulas. They therefore give mutually inverse natural maps $h_V\times_Yh_H\cong h_V\times_Oh_{O_H}$. The projection to $h_H$ is $h_p\circ h_q$ by these formulas.

source.place: Tag 02WK (lemma-composition-representable-transformations-property): explicit scheme-test pullback calculation filling its omitted proof in this case.

proof.text: For this $W$, step 3 gives that $p$ is etale and step 4 gives that $q$ is etale. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] gives that $p\circ q:W\to H$ is etale. Thus every scheme test of $jv$ is represented by $W$ with etale projection, exactly representable etaleness in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Step 4 gives the stated canonical comparison and both projection descriptions.
